title: Dr. Bessie F. Lawrence International Summer Science Institute (ISSI)
organization: Weizmann Institute of Science (Davidson Institute for Science Education)
description: A four-week English-language summer science program at the Weizmann Institute in Rehovot, Israel, for talented graduating high school students (and gap-year/early-undergraduate students) from around the world. Participants spend three weeks conducting hands-on research in Institute labs across biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics and computer science, then join a field-school excursion in the Judean Desert and Negev.
selectivity_evidence: Roughly 70-80 students are selected each year from 15-17+ countries; participants are typically chosen through each home country's own competitive process (e.g., national science-competition winners, international olympiad medalists) rather than a single centralized open application.
current_cycle_label: Runs annually each summer; program is confirmed active via its Belgian 'Friends of Weizmann' chapter page, but exact 2027 application deadline and calendar dates were not found on the pages accessible during this research pass.
verification_status: Verified - official Weizmann-network pages fetched and read (wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il news article and weizmann.be/issi program page); the Institute's own davidson.org.il ISSI subpage could not be located after a site redirect, so exact current-cycle dates/deadline are not confirmed and are left null rather than guessed.
research_notes: Applications are decentralized through country-level 'Friends of Weizmann' chapters (US, Canada, Belgium, Australia, etc.) and national science-competition pipelines rather than one central portal - ORYN's matching/apply-flow logic should account for this rather than expecting a single application_url.

title: Ignite: International High School Summer Program
description: A summer program on the Technion's Haifa campus for international high school students with a strong science/engineering background who want to develop entrepreneurial and innovation skills. Combines academic enrichment with direct exposure to Israel's research and startup ecosystem, plus a social/sightseeing program.
selectivity_evidence: Program states it 'can accept only a limited number of participants' and requires a multi-document application (transcripts, motivation letter, recommendation letters, standardized test scores where available).
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle closed - application deadline was April 29, 2026 and the program ran in July 2026 (already concluded as of this research date); 2027 dates not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official Technion International pages fetched and read (program page and its requirements-timelines subpage).
research_notes: No citizenship/nationality restriction found anywhere on the official pages - program is explicitly framed as 'International High School Summer Program.' Age threshold (17+) is the main gating criterion found.

title: NYU Abu Dhabi Summer Academy
description: An 18-month university-preparation program for Emirati high school students, built around two intensive summer sessions on NYU Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Island campus plus online study and academic refresher weekends during the school year. Covers mathematics, critical thinking and writing, humanities, and leadership/public-speaking skills, fully funded by a named scholarship.
cost: Free - covered by the Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Scholarship for Outstanding High School Students
citizenship_restrictions: Emirati nationals only - applicant must hold an Emirati passport or be the child of an Emirati mother.
residency_restrictions: Must be enrolled in a UAE high school, in Grade 10 (or equivalent) at time of nomination.
selectivity_evidence: Four-stage selective admissions process: nomination by a school representative, application submission, in-person/virtual 'Selection Days' with faculty interviews and diagnostic assessments, then enrollment. No acceptance rate disclosed.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cohort's summer session just concluded (ran July 6-August 7, 2026); this is an 18-month program so the 2026-intake cohort continues into 2027 academic-year components. Next new-cohort nomination cycle not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official NYU Abu Dhabi pages fetched and read (program overview page and application-and-selection-process page).
research_notes: Strictly Emirati-nationals-only (or child of Emirati mother) - do not match to non-Emirati UAE-resident students. NYU Abu Dhabi separately runs the University Prep Program (UPP, recorded separately in this batch) which has no nationality restriction - the two should not be conflated.

title: NYU Abu Dhabi University Prep Program (UPP)
description: A free two-day, in-person, on-campus workshop at NYU Abu Dhabi that helps rising high school seniors of any nationality build a stronger Common Application, through goal-reflection exercises, application-skills workshops, and peer community-building. Open globally to students planning to apply for the relevant admissions cycle, not restricted to UAE nationals or residents.
cost: Free - program materials and meals included; travel and accommodation are not covered
selectivity_evidence: Application includes transcript review to 'assess academic strength and admissibility'; optional recommendation letter and English-proficiency scores. No acceptance rate or cohort-size cap disclosed, so this evidence is thinner than the Summer Academy's.
current_cycle_label: 2026 edition completed July 4-5, 2026 (application deadline May 25, 2026, has passed); 2027 dates not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official NYU Abu Dhabi pages fetched and read (UPP overview page and the connect.nyu.edu registration page).
research_notes: Explicitly open to students of any nationality, in contrast to NYU Abu Dhabi's Emirati-only Summer Academy (recorded separately) - useful positive example of an internationally-open UAE-based opportunity.

title: Chemical & Biological Engineering Boot Camp
description: A hands-on, three-day boot camp for high school students in AUS's chemical and biological engineering laboratories, covering fundamentals of modern chemical and biological engineering practice. One of several short subject-specific boot camps AUS's College of Engineering runs each June for Grades 10-12 students.
current_cycle_label: 2026 edition completed June 8-10, 2026. AUS runs a similar slate of subject-specific boot camps (civil, mechanical, digital supply chain, plus a Sumo Robot Competition) each June; future dates not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official AUS events page (info.aus.edu) fetched and read. Could not access the dedicated Achievement Academy 'Outreach Program' / longer Summer Youth Program page directly (repeated 403 errors on www.aus.edu), so this shorter, successfully-verified boot camp was recorded instead of the 4-week English/TOEFL/math Summer Youth Program mentioned in older press coverage.
research_notes: AUS also runs a longer 4-week 'Summer Youth Program' (academic English/TOEFL/pre-college math prep, grades 10-12) per a 2013-era press release, but its current official page repeatedly returned HTTP 403 during this research pass and could not be independently verified - flagging as a lead for a future research pass rather than including it unverified.

title: KAUST High School Summer Program (HSSP)
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
description: A highly selective international STEM program for high-achieving high school students, combining intensive on-campus learning at KAUST (Saudi Arabia) with a residential academic track at either Oxford University or the University of Cambridge. Covers mathematics, programming, physics, chemistry, biology, AI, engineering and data science.
cost: SAR 35,000 (Oxford track) or SAR 40,000 (Cambridge track), plus a SAR 200 non-refundable application fee; covers flights, accommodation, meals, tuition, materials, activities and mentorship.
selectivity_evidence: Self-described 'highly selective international program'; multi-stage process with online interviews for shortlisted candidates only, feeding into a small cohort split across Oxford and Cambridge residential tracks.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cohort: applications closed May 14, 2026; Oxford track ran July 10-August 1, 2026, Cambridge track runs August 1-22, 2026 (concluding within days of this research date). 2027 cycle not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official KAUST Academy page fetched and read.
research_notes: No nationality/citizenship restriction found - contrasts with KAUST's other two pre-university programs in this batch (SRSI, STEPs), which are explicitly Saudi-nationals-only. This is a paid program (no fee waiver/aid mentioned) unlike SRSI and STEPs, which are fully funded.

title: Saudi Research Science Institute (SRSI)
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
description: A six-week program at KAUST blending advanced STEM coursework with supervised laboratory research - described as the first program of its kind in Saudi Arabia. Restricted to Saudi national students in Grade 11.
cost: SAR 200 non-refundable application fee; program tuition/cost itself not disclosed on the page accessed
selectivity_evidence: Selection committee evaluates academic performance, application responses, recommendation letters, a personal interview, English proficiency and test results; program states it has served 604 students total over 14 years (roughly 40-45 per year) from the national pool of Saudi Grade-11 students.
current_cycle_label: 2026 application cycle closed January 15, 2026 (hard cutoff January 22 for fee/document completion); 6-week program held over the 2026 summer. 2027 cycle not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official KAUST Academy page fetched and read.
research_notes: Explicitly Saudi-nationals-only, Grade 11 only - not eligible for international or expatriate-resident students in Saudi Arabia. Distinct from KAUST's HSSP (this batch, record 06), which has no nationality restriction.

title: STEPs (KAUST Academy College Preparation Program)
organization: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
description: A 10-month, fully-funded college-preparation pathway for Saudi Grade 10 students, combining online components, a summer program, and a fall program, designed to prepare participants for admission to top global universities.
cost: Free - fully funded including accommodation and meals; SAR 200 non-refundable application fee
selectivity_evidence: Competitive admissions test (90 minutes, math and science) followed by a personal interview, for a fully-funded 10-month place.
current_cycle_label: 2025-26 cohort: registration closed March 26, 2026, admissions test March 31, results late April; online phase April-June 2026, summer phase July-August 2026, fall phase November 2026 (program in progress as of this research date). Next admissions cycle not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official KAUST Academy page fetched and read.
research_notes: Saudi-students-only (grade 10). Note this is a 10-month program spanning three phases (online, summer, fall) rather than a single summer block - ORYN's deadline-engine logic should treat it as an extended program rather than a short camp.

title: SPAAC Summer Program
description: A one- to two-week campus-residential program at the American University of Beirut for students aged 14-18 from around the world, run by AUB's Continuing Education Center with its alumni association. Combines Arabic language and Lebanese-culture instruction with electives such as design, acting, game development, mobile app development and engineering exploration, plus supervised excursions to historical sites across Lebanon.
cost: Not finalized at time of research ('TBD' on the official page for all four track/accommodation combinations); fee is stated to include tuition, medical insurance, gym access, meals and activities/trips.
current_cycle_label: AUB's broader family of pre-university summer programs (including SPAAC) run in July each year, per the general Summer@AUB page for 2026; the SPAAC-specific page did not list exact 2026 dates or pricing at the time of this research pass.
verification_status: Verified - official AUB pages fetched and read (SPAAC program page and the general Summer@AUB pre-university programs page); exact dates, pricing and selectivity mechanism were not published on either page at the time of the fetch, so those fields are left null/unknown rather than guessed.
research_notes: Explicitly open to students 'from around the world' ages 14-18 with no citizenship restriction stated - good genuinely-international candidate. On-campus accommodation is explicitly offered to international students per AUB's general summer-programs page. No competitive-selection mechanism was described (marketing language like 'bright and motivated' only), so selectivity_tier is left unknown rather than assumed.

title: College Bound: AUC Pre-College Program
description: A three-week pre-college summer program at the American University in Cairo for students entering grades 10-12. Participants choose from AUC freshman-level courses (computer/data science, architecture, graphic design, business, entrepreneurship, political science, psychology, media studies, Arabic) taught by AUC faculty, with credit transferable if the student later enrolls at AUC.
current_cycle_label: The Summer@AUC 2026 edition of College Bound has already concluded ('has come to an end. See you next summer in 2027!' per the official page); 2027 dates/deadline not yet posted.
verification_status: Verified - official AUC page fetched and read.
research_notes: Page describes a diverse/international student body but does not state an explicit eligibility rule on nationality; no tuition, fee, or selection-process information was published on the page accessed, so cost and selectivity are left null/unknown rather than guessed.

title: Georgetown Pre-College Summer (GPS) Program
description: A three-week full-time summer program at Georgetown University in Qatar giving local students a head start on the university application process - International Relations coursework taught by Georgetown graduates, with an optional SAT-preparation track taught by Princeton Review-certified instructors, plus co-curricular sessions led by current Georgetown students.
cost: QAR 3,700 (with SAT-prep track) or QAR 1,850 (without SAT-prep track)
citizenship_restrictions: Program explicitly targets 'local students in Qatar'; preference criteria require applicants to be a Qatar national or resident.
residency_restrictions: Must be a Qatar resident (or national); entering the final two years of secondary school.
selectivity_evidence: Preference given based on academic standing (GPA 3.0/B or 80%+ overall average), solid English proficiency, and grade level; not a stated hard acceptance rate.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cycle closed - program ran July 4-23, 2026 with an application deadline of April 30, 2026 (both already passed as of this research date); 2027 dates not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official Georgetown University in Qatar page fetched and read.
research_notes: Restricted to Qatar nationals/residents - NOT internationally open, despite being hosted by a well-known international university brand. Included specifically because the task asked for Qatar/Gulf coverage and because getting this restriction right matters more than omitting a real, well-documented program.

title: Young Scholars Programme (YSP)
description: A certified, residential pre-college summer programme at Ashoka University (India) for students entering grades 9-12, offering interdisciplinary streams across the liberal arts and sciences: Foundations of Liberal Arts & Sciences, Frontiers of Science, and Tech/Data/Computer Science, among others including economics, psychology, policy and entrepreneurship.
selectivity_evidence: Application requires submission of high-school marks/transcripts and a written essay demonstrating intellectual curiosity; rolling admission explicitly described as processed against 'limited seats.' No acceptance rate disclosed.
current_cycle_label: 2026 offered two editions - May 18-29, 2026 and June 1-12, 2026 - both already completed as of this research date; 2027 dates not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official Ashoka University page (ashoka.edu.in/ysp/) fetched and read directly; a companion FAQ subpage (highschool.ashoka.edu.in/faq.aspx) that reportedly confirms international eligibility explicitly could not be fetched due to an SSL certificate error, so that specific claim is corroborated only by secondary search-indexed excerpts of that same FAQ page, not a fresh direct fetch.
research_notes: Multiple independent secondary sources (program-affiliated blog posts, education directories) consistently state 'students from throughout India and across the world are eligible to apply' - flagged here as high-confidence but not 100% independently confirmed via direct fetch of the FAQ page itself, per the verification discipline for this batch.

title: AUW Math and Science Summer School
description: A four-week, Chevron-sponsored STEM summer school at the Asian University for Women's Chattogram campus for female Bangladeshi high school students, covering mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer coding and public health, taught by international faculty from institutions including Oxford, MIT and the University of Dhaka. Top performers receive the AUW-Chevron Emerging Women Leader in STEM Award.
citizenship_restrictions: Female students who are residents of Bangladesh only, who have completed SSC/O-level or HSC/A-level.
selectivity_evidence: Explicitly described as highly selective, with exactly 80 students selected each year from a Bangladesh-wide applicant pool based on academic performance, extracurricular involvement, and demonstrated STEM commitment.
current_cycle_label: 2026 cohort's program ran July 20-August 20, 2026 (concluded the day before this research date); application deadline for that cycle was June 30, 2026. 2027 cycle not yet announced.
verification_status: Verified - official Asian University for Women page fetched and read.
research_notes: Restricted to female Bangladeshi residents only (gender restriction has no dedicated schema field in this batch's contract - recorded in citizenship_restrictions and here). Genuinely selective and well-documented rather than a generic domestic olympiad feeder, which is why it was included despite the residency restriction.

title: UAE Hackathon - Rising Stars Track
description: The school-students track of the UAE Hackathon, a national innovation initiative now in its ninth edition. Teams of 2-7 students aged 11-17 build prototypes addressing national-challenge themes, competing through regional hackathon events toward a national Innovation Summit and Awards Ceremony.
residency_restrictions: Participation is explicitly limited to participants residing within the UAE with a valid Emirates ID - not open to non-UAE-resident international applicants.
selectivity_evidence: Entry is via open team registration (through a UAE PASS account), but advancing to the Innovation Summit and winning awards is a judged, competitive outcome rather than a gated application process.
current_cycle_label: 2026 edition is upcoming as of this research date: regional hackathons run October 19-29, 2026, with the Innovation Summit and Awards Ceremony on November 11, 2026 (the official FAQ page also references post-hackathon support continuing November 16-27, 2026).
verification_status: Verified - official UAE Hackathon FAQ page (hackathon.ae/en/FAQs) fetched and read.
research_notes: Residency-restricted (must live in the UAE with an Emirates ID) rather than nationality-restricted - open to any nationality of resident, but not to a student applying from outside the UAE. This is the one record in this batch with a currently upcoming (not yet closed) cycle.

title: SparkTank
description: Pakistan's first business incubator/competition for students aged 10-19, open to students at any public or private school across Pakistan regardless of school affiliation. Selected teams (individuals or groups of up to 4) receive a zero-fee incubation period to develop a business concept, judged on viability and potential for positive social impact.
residency_restrictions: Must attend a school (public or private) in Pakistan.
selectivity_evidence: Only 10 projects are enrolled per cohort, selected on 'viability of the concept' and 'potential to create a positive social impact.'
current_cycle_label: Runs two cohorts per year on a rolling basis; specific 2026/2027 cohort application windows were not published on the pages accessed during this research pass (program materials show some internal inconsistency between a stated '5-month' and a '3-month plus extension' incubation length).
verification_status: Verified - official SparkTank page fetched and read.
research_notes: Pakistan-school-based only, not internationally open, but a genuine distinctive selective entrepreneurship program (not a repetitive olympiad feeder) - included for category breadth (entrepreneurship) and to begin closing Pakistan's zero-coverage gap.

title: ROTA Programme
description: An ongoing youth-and-young-adult volunteering programme run by Qatar's Education Above All Foundation, supporting EAA events, partner-led events, and longer-term volunteer commitments tied to the Foundation's national and international education initiatives.
current_cycle_label: Rolling/ongoing volunteer registration with no fixed application cycle or deadline.
verification_status: Verified - official Education Above All Foundation page fetched and read.
research_notes: Thin on specifics beyond a general registration form - no defined cohort, deadline, or dedicated teen-focused track was found (stated age range 15-35 is broader than ORYN's core 14-18 audience). Included mainly to close the volunteering-category and Qatar-breadth gaps with a real, verified, currently-open opportunity; flagging lower confidence in its day-to-day relevance versus the other records in this batch.
